metadata: Editorial biographies written from archived league evidence. Trade picks are audited measured direct-outcome candidates, not universal process grades. Waiver candidates are ranked from verified completed Sleeper adds/waivers matched to subsequent credited regular-season starts; source coverage remains incomplete before 2020 and for some roster-seat histories.

Stilly.biography:
Stilly has spent a decade proving that a franchise is never finished being built. One of the Fellas' original four managers in 2016, he survived years of middling records, then finally turned an 8–6 regular season in 2023 into his first championship. It was the breakthrough that changed how his career had to be judged.

One of the decisive moves during the 2023 championship run came on October 26, 2023: Stilly sent Cooper Kupp to Tony and received Mike Evans and Derrick Henry. That is the transaction behind the shorthand about a late-season roster reshuffle. It added two players in return for one, but the archived trade receipt alone does not establish how much of the eventual championship should be credited to the deal.

Stilly returned to the championship game in 2024, finishing runner-up, after another busy stretch of roster construction. On September 24, 2024, he sent Christian McCaffrey, Diontae Johnson and Tee Higgins to Tom in exchange for Terry McLaurin, De'Von Achane and Tank Dell. Eight days later, on October 2, 2024, he traded Jordan Love to Tom for Chase Brown. The preserved trade-production snapshot credits Brown with 154.4 starter points in 10 starts after that acquisition. Rather than a vague 'Chase Brown chapter,' this was a documented quarterback-for-running-back exchange in the middle of Stilly's second consecutive championship-game season. Jayden Daniels, whom Stilly drafted in 2024 and later retained as a 2026 keeper, was another piece of the longer-term roster plan.

The pattern was not simply 'making lots of moves.' In 2023 Stilly consolidated Cooper Kupp into two established players. In 2024 he turned one high-profile three-player package into a new group and then swapped a quarterback for an additional running back. Those moves provide meaningful context for his 66–77 career regular-season record, championship and runner-up finish, without pretending a retrospective starter-point comparison proves any one trade was a winning decision.

A second defining chapter began on November 12, 2025. In a completed three-team deal with JMid and Tom, Stilly acquired Amon-Ra St. Brown alongside Jordan Addison and Jared Goff. That move enabled him to select Amon-Ra as a 2026 keeper. On October 7, 2026, he then traded with JMid again to reacquire Ja'Marr Chase, receiving Chase and Devaughn Vele while JMid's recorded side received Davante Adams, George Kittle and Breece Hall. The 2026 keeper ledger confirms seven Amon-Ra starts and 113.5 starter points through Week 8. This is a meaningful cross-season strategy story, not evidence of a certified trade win or a completed 2026 season.

The earlier title run remains the foundation of his résumé: a founding manager who kept rebuilding reached two consecutive championship games, winning one. The 2025 three-team deal shows how that same approach carried into a new keeper-era chapter.
Stilly.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Kirk Cousins (2021) currently leads at +55.20 above the positional starter benchmark.

JMid.biography:
JMid joined the Fellas after the 2023 season, replacing Evans as the manager of that franchise slot. His first official season was 2024, when the team scored a league-leading 1,730.22 points but finished 8–6. That impressive scoring output showed potential, even as the final standings demonstrated how little a high points total guarantees.

The 2025 campaign finished 5–9. On September 17, 2024, JMid traded with Stew: JMid's recorded receiving side was Calvin Ridley and Kyren Williams, while Stew received James Cook. That's a documented example of JMid changing the mix of his roster in his debut season. Later lineups included Joe Burrow and Ja'Marr Chase, but those player appearances are not automatically proof of how either was acquired. These examples describe documented personnel history rather than an all-encompassing grade for his decisions.

At 16–20 through Week 8 of 2026, JMid is still looking for his first championship. His résumé begins in 2024; Evans retains the 2023 team results, postseason finish, and corresponding historical records.
JMid.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Rico Dowdle (2025) currently leads at +50.99 above the positional starter benchmark.

Tom.biography:
The Fellas' championship history begins with Thommy. One of the four managers who founded the league in 2016, he claimed the first three titles in succession, turning the ESPN years into a personal dynasty before anyone else could establish one. After the 2018 three-peat, the regular seasons were far less imposing: a 2–11 season in 2019, followed by several losing campaigns, gave rivals reason to wonder whether the early reign belonged to another era.

The answer came in 2024. Thommy went 9–5 and won a fourth championship, six seasons after the third, making his trophy case the standard against which every other manager is measured. His 67–75–1 regular-season record is striking precisely because it does not look like a four-time champion's record.

That contradiction is the biography: Thommy has not controlled every autumn, but when the league recounts the seasons that ended with someone holding the trophy, his name appears more often than anyone else's.
Tom.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Elijah Mitchell (2021) currently leads at +64.49 above the positional starter benchmark.

Stew.biography:
Stew has been part of the Fellas since the first season in 2016, and few franchises better capture the promise and danger of refusing to leave a roster alone. His 2019 team went 9–4; the 2021 version collapsed to 3–11. Then came 2022, the high-water mark of his regular-season career: an 11–3 finish with the league's best points and potential points.

Two 2022 trades show exactly how he approached roster construction. On September 27, 2022, Stew acquired Justin Jefferson and Cordarrelle Patterson from Evans in exchange for the recorded receiving package of Mike Williams, James Conner and James Robinson. On November 10, 2022, Stew acquired Ja'Marr Chase from Birch, whose recorded side received Cordarrelle Patterson, Jeff Wilson and Chase Claypool. Those transactions help explain how Stew concentrated talent in a season when he went 11–3, though the archive does not prove that either exchange caused the record or would have been judged fairly at the time. But another 3–11 season followed in 2023, leaving a career defined by huge swings rather than gradual progression. Stew's 67–76 record does not tell you how intimidating his best teams have been, and his championship total—still zero—does not erase the quality of that 2022 roster.

What remains unresolved is whether the manager who has repeatedly demonstrated the ability to assemble an elite team can carry one through the final playoff week.
Stew.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Jamaal Williams (2022) currently leads at +61.77 above the positional starter benchmark.

Scott.biography:
Scott did not need a decade to make himself part of league history. His recorded Fellas tenure began in 2024 with a 5–9 season, hardly an arrival that suggested an immediate championship. One year later, the script flipped. An 8–6 regular season in 2025 became a title-winning run, completed with a commanding championship-game victory.

Bijan Robinson and James Cook are among the players whose recorded lineup production helped define the franchise's rise. The contrast is almost the entire story: a newcomer endured an unremarkable first campaign, adjusted, and collected a trophy before several far more established managers.

At 17–19 through Week 8 of 2026, Scott still has the shortest regular-season résumé among the current group. That makes his legacy unusually difficult to rank by volume alone. He has already accomplished the hardest thing in fantasy football; the question is whether the 2025 breakthrough becomes the opening chapter of a long contender's career or remains one spectacular season.
Scott.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Jauan Jennings (2024) currently leads at +42.77 above the positional starter benchmark.

Mitch.biography:
Mitch entered the Fellas in 2018 and has built the strongest regular-season winning percentage among the current managers with a substantial multi-year record. His climb was visible early: consecutive 9–4 seasons in 2019 and 2020 established him as a recurring contender. The extraordinary peak came in 2025, when he went 13–1 and scored 1,894.88 points.

Even that season could not deliver the missing championship. Then he opened 2026 with eight straight wins, extending a stretch of week-to-week dominance that few managers in league history can match. Players such as Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Josh Allen and Jonathan Taylor have appeared in his recorded roster story, but the unmistakable through-line is the results: 71–46 in the regular season and a habit of making opponents chase him in the standings.

For Mitch, greatness is no longer a question of whether he can build a winning team. His entire career has become a pursuit of the one trophy that has somehow remained beyond those records.
Mitch.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Tyler Lockett (2022) currently leads at +96.22 above the positional starter benchmark.

Tony.biography:
Tony's place in the league is grounded in consistency, interrupted by a season that made everything count. After joining the recorded league in 2017, he put together consecutive 8–5 campaigns in 2018 and 2019, stumbled to 4–10 in 2020, then rebounded spectacularly. The 2021 team went 10–3 and finished the job with a championship.

Since then, another 10–4 campaign in 2023 has reinforced that the title was no accident of a single lucky roster. His championship season includes a particularly clear front-office example: on October 5, 2021, Tony received Joe Mixon from Koble, whose side received Zack Moss and James Robinson. Two years later, on October 26, 2023, Tony sent Mike Evans and Derrick Henry to Stilly to acquire Cooper Kupp. Both deals identify actual counterparties and incoming assets; the recorded post-trade starter points are not, by themselves, a verdict on either manager's decision.

The 72–57 regular-season mark is among the most substantial winning résumés in the current league. Tony's story is not one of a franchise permanently on top or endlessly rebuilding; it is of a manager who repeatedly returns to contention, with 2021 as the proof that he knows how to finish.
Tony.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: James Robinson (2020) currently leads at +141.68 above the positional starter benchmark.

Stover.biography:
Before he was Gurt, Stover was the manager behind the PurpleHeaded YogurtSlingers, one of the original franchises of 2016. The team names changed, but the career stayed continuous. He endured uneven early seasons, built an 11–3 regular-season powerhouse in 2021, and won his first championship in 2022 after a 9–5 campaign.

That title was followed by another strong high point in 2024, when he posted a 10–4 record without adding a second trophy. The personnel archive includes Brian Thomas Jr. as a documented 2024 draft value. A recorded September 12, 2024 trade with Stew also shows Stover receiving Davante Adams while Stew received Malik Nabers. The exchange gives a concrete example of his front-office activity without treating a later points snapshot as a final judgment. Nico Collins also appears in the broader roster record, though this biography does not assign him an acquisition method without a linked transaction.

Through Week 8 of 2026, Stover stands at 75–68, with more regular-season victories than any other current manager. His legacy is not tied to one hot postseason. Across the ESPN beginnings, the Sleeper years and changing franchise identities, he has accumulated the kind of long-running, title-backed career that gives the league its history.
Stover.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Philadelphia Eagles D/ST (2022) currently leads at +83.83 above the positional starter benchmark.

Kuhl.biography:
Kuhl's best seasons prove he has been capable of competing with anyone: 9–5 in 2020, an 8–6 playoff-caliber year in 2022, and several early campaigns above .500. Yet the longer arc has been far harsher. A 5–9 season in 2021 was followed by three more 5–9 finishes from 2023 through 2025, with an 8–6 rebound in 2022 separating the slumps.

Then came an 0–8 start in 2026. The 51–67 career mark captures the accumulated damage, but not every smart decision along the way. One concrete example of his willingness to reshape a roster came on September 27, 2023. In a deal with Stew, Kuhl received James Conner, De'Von Achane and Puka Nacua while Stew received CeeDee Lamb and Travis Etienne Jr. The record establishes the exchange, not an indisputable winner; Kuhl finished that season 5–9. Earlier, on September 27, 2021, Kuhl received Leonard Fournette, Patrick Mahomes and Brandon Aiyuk in a trade with Evans, whose recorded side received Aaron Rodgers and Keenan Allen.

Kuhl's career has become a case study in the difference between finding useful players and assembling enough winning weeks. He has flashes of sound roster construction and seasons that suggested a breakthrough. What he lacks is the sustained run—and the championship—that would change how the league remembers him.
Kuhl.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Kyren Williams (2023) currently leads at +72.25 above the positional starter benchmark.

Birch.biography:
Birch joined the Fellas in 2017 as Hogan's Heroes and wasted little time becoming a problem for the rest of the league. He reached the championship game in 2018, then stormed through 2019 at 11–2 and won his first title. The 2020 season remained strong at 9–4, and in 2021 he repeated the remarkable 11–2 regular-season mark.

Across those three seasons, Birch went 31–8, creating one of the most convincing sustained stretches in the archive. The roster history highlights Josh Allen and Justin Jefferson among his productive lineup mainstays, while the front-office record supplies a separate catalog of trades and draft decisions.

Since that peak, his results have been more uneven, including a run of .500 seasons and a 6–8 finish in 2025. At 72–56 through Week 8 of 2026, Birch still owns one of the league's best long-term winning percentages. His career will always begin with the 2019 championship, but the true weight of his résumé is how consistently dangerous his teams were around it.
Birch.waiverStatus: Ranked from verified completed Sleeper acquisitions matched to subsequent credited starts: Aaron Rodgers (2020) currently leads at +90.05 above the positional starter benchmark.
